io.milvus.common.utils

Class BloomFilterUtils.Builder

  • java.lang.Object
    • io.milvus.common.utils.BloomFilterUtils.Builder
  • Enclosing class:
    BloomFilterUtils

    public static class BloomFilterUtils.Builder
extends Object
    Incrementally constructs an SBBF and serializes it into an MBF1 envelope. Not thread-safe.

    Prefer this over BloomFilterUtils.buildBloomFilter(List, double) for very large membership sets: addInt64(long) takes a primitive, so a 10M-member filter costs no boxed List<Long> (which would be roughly 240 MB of Long objects on its own).

    Unlike the convenience method, a Builder accepts both domains, which produces a filter that matches integer and string members alike.

    • Constructor Detail

      • Builder

        public Builder(long n,
               double fpr)
        Creates a builder sized for n distinct values at false-positive rate fpr.
        Parameters:
        n - the expected number of distinct members; it only drives sizing, so inserting more is allowed and simply raises the effective false-positive rate
        fpr - the false-positive rate, in [BloomFilterUtils.MIN_FPR, BloomFilterUtils.MAX_FPR]
        Throws:
        MilvusClientException - if n is negative or fpr is out of range

      • build

        public byte[] build()
        Stamps the MBF1 header onto the filter and returns the envelope.

        The returned array is the Builder's own buffer, not a copy — a filter therefore costs one allocation of its final size rather than a body plus an equal-sized serialization buffer, which matters at 64 MiB. Treat it as read-only, and copy it if you keep inserting afterwards: a later add mutates an array already handed out. Calling build() repeatedly is fine; each call re-stamps the header.

        Returns:
        the MBF1 filter envelope
